summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with primary central nervous system lymphoma was admitted for her 23rd cycle of high-dose methotrexate chemotherapy. She reported feeling well prior to admission with no neurological symptoms, fever, or pain. Methotrexate was administered safely after urine alkalinization, and leucovorin rescue was initiated 24 hours post-infusion. She experienced nausea and vomiting during the first day after treatment but improved by discharge, tolerating a regular diet. Methotrexate levels declined appropriately to 0.03 micromolar. Her chronic conditions, including ulcerative colitis, asthma, depression, and chemotherapy-induced anemia, were stable and managed without complication. Aspirin was restarted at discharge. She was discharged home in stable condition with a short course of oral leucovorin and a plan to return in one month for her next cycle.
problems: Primary central nervous system lymphoma, unspecified site, extranodal and solid organ sites
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
Antineoplastic and immunosuppressive drugs causing adverse effects in therapeutic use
